trust_decision.summary: Which admin-account fields (role_id, and by extension other privilege columns) a logged-in back-office admin may set when saving an admin account; at the pinned commit admin/user/save only checks 'edit self or has edit_other_admin' and then copies the whole POST['admin'] array into the admin table, filtered only to table columns.

landing_point.why: Advisory title names admin/user/save; the admin/user route is Vvveb\Controller\Admin\User (admin/controller/admin/user.php:28) which inherits save() from the shared user controller.

fix_sites.entry_point: HTTP admin back office index.php?module=admin/user&action=save (create and update branches)
fix_sites.module_kind: admin controller (shared base class for user and admin types)

fix_sites.entry_point: same route; removal of the second read of POST that would overwrite the filtered array

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Both changed lines are in admin/controller/user/user.php save(); the second commit (public/js/app.js) is an unrelated theme JS change.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: For REST /rest/admin/#admin_id#: default roles below super_admin deny 'admin/*' (install/sql/insert/admin/role.sql:3), so it looks like a super_admin-only API. For site_access: the advisory names only role_id, and an empty site_access is a legitimate 'all sites' value.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Authors, contributors and site admins must still be able to edit their own profile through admin/user/save (granted in role.sql). super_admin must still be able to assign any role, including super_admin, and admin can assign roles >= 2. An empty site_access means 'all sites' in the site picker, so stripping or forcing site_access breaks legitimate saves.

O6_input_shapes: role_id present for a non-admin role (unset)
role_id present for role 'admin' (clamped with max(role_id, 2))
both create (no admin_id) and update (admin_id) branches, because the check sits before the branch split
removes the second $this->request->post read so the filtered array is the one that gets saved

O7_producer.where: admin/sql/mysqli/admin.sql:146 and admin/sql/mysqli/admin.sql:168 (@FILTER(:admin, admin) allowlists every admin table column, including role_id, site_access, status and token, from install/sql/mysqli/schema/admin/admin.sql:17-21)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: REST generic CRUD on the admin table (POST/PATCH/PUT /rest/admin and /rest/admin/#admin_id#) writes the raw request body, including admin[role_id], through model('admin')->edit/add with no role check.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Only the generic route permission check (rest/controller/base.php:142-148) applies, and default non-super roles deny admin/*. It reads as a super_admin-only API, a different app (rest/) and a generic CRUD that is not the admin/user/save named in the advisory.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: rest/controller/crud.php:78-96 -> system/traits/crud.php:103-138; another app directory (rest/) plus system/traits, 2 packages from the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Self-edit via admin/user/save still lets a non-admin role (author, contributor, site_admin) set its own site_access, another privilege column. The published fix only touches role_id.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory and fix name role_id only. site_access looks like a profile preference, and an empty or unset value is legitimately turned into '[]' (= all sites in admin/component/sites.php:55-58).
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the landing point; the meaning of the value lives in admin/component/sites.php and admin/controller/settings/sites.php:88-92

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A 'change role' action or profile endpoint that calls the unused setRole procedure with a role *name* (role = 'super_admin') and resolves it to role_id after a numeric role_id check.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: setRole already exists with both role and role_id inputs and has no caller, so a maintainer wiring up a role dropdown by name is plausible. It is a how-type identity differential (name vs id).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Admin::update/add accept arbitrary keys. A second caller (for example a profile or 'my account' controller, or an import) passing request data straight through would bypass a controller-only fix.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Admin::update is already called from three other places (admin/controller/user/reset.php:48, :84; install/controller/index.php:272) with partial arrays, so another thin caller is natural.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A schema-specific REST controller for 'admin' (like rest/controller/cart/cart.php) that maps a 'role' field onto role_id.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The REST app already has per-schema controllers alongside the generic CRUD.
